title: Enzyme treatment and gas production
bodyMd:
A class measured oxygen released when a plant extract was mixed with hydrogen peroxide. Each assay used the same total liquid volume, peroxide concentration and reaction temperature. Gas was collected in a graduated tube for60s. Three replicate assays were performed per condition; all showed the same ordering, and their mean gas volumes appear below.

Experiment1 varied untreated extract volume. Distilled water was added so the total assay volume stayed constant.

| Extract volume (mL) | Gas volume after60s (mL) |
|---:|---:|
|0|1|
|1|7|
|2|13|
|3|19|

In Experiment2,2mL of extract was either untreated, heated to90degrees C for10min and cooled, or heated identically and then supplemented with1mL fresh extract. Every final assay had the same total volume and peroxide concentration.

| Treatment | Mean gas volume (mL) |
|---|---:|
|Untreated2mL extract|13|
|Heated2mL extract|2|
|Heated2mL plus1mL fresh extract|8|

The class considered whether a heat-sensitive substance in the extract promoted gas formation. An enzyme is a protein catalyst; heating can alter the structure needed for its catalytic activity.
